Bacterial vs human chromosome
cards.a: Bacterial: CIRCULAR, ONE origin, haploid, polyamines. Human: LINEAR, MANY origins, diploid, histones, telomeres.
cards.why: No ends means no telomeres. Human chromosomes have ends.

cards.q: Plasmid vs transposon
cards.a: PLASMID replicates on its own. TRANSPOSON cannot; it must insert into a replicon.
cards.why: If a transposon could copy itself it would not need to jump.

cards.q: Natural vs artificial competence
cards.a: NATURAL: the cell's own genes, transient window. ARTIFICIAL: CaCl2 or electroporation in the lab.
cards.why: 'Its own regulatory genes' in a stem always means natural.

cards.q: Core vs holoenzyme
cards.a: HOLOENZYME = core + sigma. Core alone writes RNA but cannot find a promoter.
cards.why: Holoenzyme is the bigger assembly; sigma is the add-on.

cards.q: Where sigma acts
cards.a: Sigma acts on DNA at the PROMOTER. Never on a ribosome.
cards.why: A new sigma changes which genes are transcribed, and only later which proteins appear.

cards.q: Which rRNA in which subunit
cards.why: Big rRNAs in the big piece. 16S is small and is the ID marker.

cards.q: F+ vs Hfr
cards.a: F+: F is free, transfers itself, recipient becomes F+. Hfr: F is integrated, chromosome transfers, recipient stays F−.
cards.why: Free F travels. Integrated F enters last and the bridge breaks first.

cards.q: Inducible vs repressible
cards.a: INDUCIBLE: normally OFF, signal turns ON, catabolic (lac). REPRESSIBLE: normally ON, signal turns OFF, anabolic (trp).
cards.why: Eat it = off until food arrives. Make it = on until you have enough.

cards.q: Inducer vs corepressor
cards.a: INDUCER inactivates a repressor (ON). COREPRESSOR activates a repressor (OFF).
cards.why: Allolactose removes the lac repressor. Tryptophan arms the trp repressor.

cards.q: Repressor vs attenuation in trp
cards.a: REPRESSOR blocks initiation (DNA level). ATTENUATION blocks completion (RNA level, leader hairpin).
cards.why: Two brakes: one before the car starts, one mid-drive.

cards.q: Gram positive vs negative wall
cards.a: POSITIVE: thick PG (40 layers), teichoic acids, NO outer membrane. NEGATIVE: thin PG (1-2 layers), outer membrane, LPS, periplasm.
cards.why: Only negatives wear a raincoat. Only positives have teichoic acids.

cards.q: Gram stain colours
cards.why: Positive keeps the first dye. Negative loses it and takes safranin.

cards.q: Lysine vs DAP
cards.a: L-LYSINE at position 3 in Gram POSITIVE PG (with pentaglycine bridge). meso-DAP in Gram NEGATIVE PG (direct link).
cards.why: S. aureus uses lysine + glycine bridge. E. coli uses DAP.

cards.q: Endotoxin vs exotoxin
cards.a: ENDOTOXIN: LPS lipid A, structural, Gram negative only, heat stable. EXOTOXIN: secreted protein, heat labile, both groups.
cards.why: Endo = inside as part of the cell. Exo = exported.

cards.q: Lipid A vs O antigen
cards.a: LIPID A = toxic, membrane anchor, essential. O ANTIGEN = outer, variable, serotyping.
cards.why: Toxicity is at the base, identity is at the tip.

cards.q: Protoplast vs spheroplast
cards.a: PROTOPLAST = wall-less Gram POSITIVE. SPHEROPLAST = wall-less Gram NEGATIVE.
cards.why: Spheroplast keeps some outer membrane, so it is the negative.

cards.q: Gap vs nick
cards.a: GAP: nucleotides MISSING, Pol I fills. NICK: BOND missing, ligase seals.
cards.why: Ligase makes bonds, not nucleotides.

cards.q: Pol I vs Pol III
cards.a: POL III builds the bulk of the new strand. POL I removes RNA primers and fills gaps.
cards.why: Bigger number, bigger job.

cards.q: Generalised vs specialised transduction
cards.a: GENERALISED: lytic, ANY gene, random packaging. SPECIALISED: lysogenic/temperate, only genes ADJACENT to the prophage.
cards.why: General = any. Special = location-specific.

cards.q: Transformation vs conjugation by test
cards.a: DNase kills TRANSFORMATION. Contact-blocking filter kills CONJUGATION. Transduction survives both.
cards.why: Only transformation exposes DNA to the medium.

cards.q: Prototroph vs auxotroph
cards.a: PROTOTROPH grows on minimal medium. AUXOTROPH needs a nutrient supplied.
cards.why: Auxo = needs auxiliary help.

cards.q: Autotroph vs heterotroph
cards.a: AUTOTROPH uses CO2. HETEROTROPH uses organic carbon. Pathogens are heterotrophs.
cards.why: Different axis from proto/auxotroph: this one is about carbon source.

cards.q: Aerotolerant vs microaerophile
cards.a: AEROTOLERANT: cannot use oxygen, unharmed by it (S. pneumoniae). MICROAEROPHILE: REQUIRES a little oxygen (C. jejuni).
cards.why: Tolerate vs need.

cards.q: Facultative vs aerotolerant
cards.a: FACULTATIVE uses oxygen when present, ferments without it. AEROTOLERANT never uses oxygen.
cards.why: Facultative has a choice. Aerotolerant has no aerobic option.

cards.q: Selective vs differential media
cards.a: SELECTIVE controls WHO grows. DIFFERENTIAL controls what you can SEE.
cards.why: MSA is both: salt selects, mannitol/phenol red differentiates.

cards.q: Defined vs complex media
cards.a: DEFINED (minimal): exact composition known. COMPLEX: undefined extracts like blood or yeast.
cards.why: Fastidious pathogens need complex.

cards.q: Bactericidal vs bacteriostatic
cards.a: CIDAL kills. STATIC pauses growth and needs the immune system to finish.
cards.why: Static is a poor choice in a neutropenic patient.

cards.q: MIC vs MBC
cards.a: MIC = lowest concentration that INHIBITS. MBC = lowest that KILLS 99.9%.
cards.why: I for inhibit, B for bactericidal.

cards.q: MRSA vs beta-lactamase
cards.a: MRSA = mecA / PBP2a, an ALTERED TARGET. Beta-lactamase = DESTROYS the drug.
cards.why: MRSA changes the lock. Beta-lactamase breaks the key.

cards.q: Beta-lactam vs vancomycin target
cards.a: BETA-LACTAM binds the ENZYME (PBP). VANCOMYCIN binds the SUBSTRATE (D-Ala-D-Ala).
cards.why: VRE changes D-Ala-D-Ala to D-Ala-D-Lac, which only matters if the drug binds substrate.

cards.q: Bacitracin vs beta-lactam step
cards.a: BACITRACIN blocks bactoprenol RECYCLING (carrier). BETA-LACTAM blocks CROSS-LINKING (transpeptidase).
cards.why: Bacitracin acts earlier, at the delivery truck.

cards.q: Transglycosylase vs transpeptidase
cards.a: TRANSGLYCOSYLASE links SUGARS (NAG-NAM chain). TRANSPEPTIDASE links PEPTIDES (cross-links) and is the PBP.
cards.why: Glyco = sugar. Peptid = peptide.

cards.q: 30S vs 50S drugs
cards.a: 30S: Aminoglycosides, Tetracyclines (buy AT 30). 50S: Chloramphenicol, Clindamycin, Erythromycin/macrolides, Linezolid (CCEL at 50).
cards.why: Aminoglycosides misread; tetracyclines block A site; macrolides block translocation.

cards.q: Aminoglycoside vs tetracycline
cards.a: AMINOGLYCOSIDE: misreading, CIDAL, oto/nephrotoxic, no anaerobes. TETRACYCLINE: blocks A site, STATIC, photosensitivity, chelates cations.
cards.why: Same subunit, opposite lethality.

cards.q: Sulfonamide vs trimethoprim
cards.a: SULFONAMIDE = PABA analogue, dihydropteroate synthase, EARLY. TRIMETHOPRIM = DHFR, LATE.
cards.why: Sulfa comes first in the pathway and first in the name TMP-SMX reversed.

cards.q: Gyrase vs topoisomerase IV for fluoroquinolones
cards.a: GYRASE (topo II) is the target in Gram NEGATIVES. TOPO IV in Gram POSITIVES.
cards.why: Negative goes with the lower number.

cards.q: Rifampin vs fluoroquinolone target
cards.a: RIFAMPIN hits RNA polymerase (transcription). FLUOROQUINOLONES hit gyrase (replication).
cards.why: R for RNA.

cards.q: Transition vs transversion
cards.a: TRANSITION: like for like (purine↔purine). TRANSVERSION: purine↔pyrimidine.
cards.why: Transversion crosses categories.

cards.q: Missense vs nonsense
cards.a: MISSENSE = different amino acid. NONSENSE = premature STOP.
cards.why: Nonsense ends the sentence.

cards.q: Silent vs neutral
cards.a: SILENT: base changes, amino acid does NOT. NEUTRAL: amino acid changes, function does NOT.
cards.why: Silent stays quiet at the protein level; neutral speaks but changes nothing.

cards.q: Intercalator vs base analogue
cards.a: INTERCALATORS cause FRAMESHIFTS (insert/delete). BASE ANALOGUES cause POINT mutations (mispairing).
cards.why: Wedge in vs slot in.

cards.q: Nitrous acid vs nitrous oxide
cards.a: NITROUS ACID (HNO2) is the deaminating mutagen. Nitrous oxide is laughing gas.
cards.why: The transcript audio said oxide; the slide says acid. Acid is correct.

cards.q: Fluctuation test vs Ames test
cards.a: FLUCTUATION: are mutations spontaneous or induced (variance between cultures). AMES: is a chemical mutagenic (revertant counts).
cards.why: Fluctuation asks when; Ames asks whether.

cards.q: Lag vs stationary phase
cards.a: LAG: no division, high metabolism, gearing up. STATIONARY: division equals death, nutrients gone, spores and antibiotics made.
cards.why: Both flat on the curve, opposite reasons.

cards.q: Turbidity vs viable count
cards.a: TURBIDITY counts all cells, live and dead. VIABLE COUNT counts only cells that divide (CFU).
cards.why: Sterility checks need viable count.

cards.q: Capsule vs slime layer
cards.a: CAPSULE: organised, tightly bound, blocks phagocytosis. SLIME LAYER: loose, unorganised, biofilm.
cards.why: Both are outside the wall; only one is tidy.

cards.q: Fimbriae vs F pilus
cards.a: FIMBRIAE: many, short, ADHERENCE. F PILUS: few, long, CONJUGATION.
cards.why: Common pili stick; sex pili transfer.

cards.q: Spore vs vegetative cell
cards.a: SPORE: dormant, resistant, survival, one per cell. VEGETATIVE: growing, dividing, susceptible.
cards.why: Sporulation is not reproduction.

cards.q: Henle vs Koch
cards.a: HENLE proposed the germ theory criteria (1840). KOCH proved them experimentally.
cards.why: Idea first, proof second.

cards.q: Griffith vs Avery
cards.a: GRIFFITH showed something transfers. AVERY showed it is DNA.
cards.why: Phenomenon, then chemistry.
